title: Priority heatmap playbook: scenario-driven scoring for inference workloads
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a reproducible playbook that produces a scenario-driven priority heatmap for roadmap initiatives. The playbook combines RICE-style inputs with workload-specific latency/cost surfaces and user-impact scenarios to produce a ranked heatmap (initiative x scenario) to guide cycle planning and OKR alignment.
motivation: Existing prioritization decks are fragmented: PMs use subjective RICE numbers, Engs provide separate latency/cost estimates, and Platform lacks a repeatable way to compare initiatives across traffic shapes and customer tiers. A heatmap playbook will standardize inputs, surface sensitivity across scenarios, and make trade-offs visible for roadmap and Dedicated/Private planning.
scope:
- Define canonical scenario templates (e.g., bursty PLG, steady enterprise, low-latency search)
- Standardize input fields and normalization rules for reach/impact/confidence/effort (RICE) and add cost-per-token and p95 latency delta estimates
- Implement a reproducible spreadsheet and a lightweight script to compute heatmaps and Monte Carlo sensitivity
- Deliver PM-facing guidance and a one-page cheat sheet for cycle planning meetings
out_of_scope:
- Building an integrated dashboard in Console (will be a follow-up)
- Automated routing or autoscale policy changes based on heatmap output
success_metrics: Playbook adopted by ~80% of PMs in Q2 planning
Time-to-decision in roadmap reviews reduced by 30%
Top-5 prioritized initiatives show improved alignment between estimated and observed post-launch latency/cost within 20%
acceptance_criteria: Canonical scenario templates documented and approved by Eng+PM+Design
Spreadsheet and script compute heatmap for at least 10 initiatives with Monte Carlo sensitivity
A pilot cycle uses the heatmap for final prioritization and we collect retrospective feedback
Cheat sheet and a 30-minute training session delivered to PMs and Eng leads
decisions: Use three canonical scenarios (PLG-burst, Enterprise-steady, Regulated-low-latency) for initial rollout
Normalize RICE reach by monthly active users impacted, not revenue, to favor product-lever improvements
Represent cost impact as delta $/1000 tokens for each initiative's primary workload
tradeoffs: Using standardized templates reduces per-initative nuance but improves comparability
Monte Carlo increases confidence but requires better effort estimates from Eng
Heatmap ranking may overweight cost-sensitive initiatives for Dedicated customers; include filters by customer segment
